MOLECULAR CYTOGENETICS REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

Patient: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen: Lymph node biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL)

TEST PERFORMED
Interphase Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) Panel for B-Cell Lymphoma

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed using dual-color break-apart and dual fusion translocation probes on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue sections. Analysis was correlated with CD79a immunostained slides to ensure evaluation of B-cells. A total of 100 interphase nuclei were analyzed for each probe set.

Probes utilized:
- MYC (8q24) break-apart probe
- IGH/BCL2 dual fusion probe for t(14;18)
- BCL6 (3q27) break-apart probe

RESULTS

MYC (8q24) rearrangement: NEGATIVE
- No evidence of MYC rearrangement detected
- Normal signal pattern observed in 98/100 cells analyzed

IGH-BCL2 t(14;18) translocation: NEGATIVE
- No evidence of t(14;18)(q32;q21) detected
- Normal signal pattern (2F2O2G) observed in 97/100 cells analyzed

BCL6 (3q27) rearrangement: NEGATIVE
- No evidence of BCL6 rearrangement detected
- 2-3 copies of intact BCL6 signals observed in 85/100 cells
- Clinical significance of additional BCL6 copies is unclear

INTERPRETATION
FISH analysis shows no evidence of MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 gene rearrangements commonly associated with aggressive B-cell lymphomas. The presence of 2-3 copies of BCL6 without rearrangement is of uncertain significance in this DLBCL case and may represent low-level copy number gain or nuclear truncation artifact.

TECHNICAL LIMITATIONS
This method cannot detect cryptic insertion events, which may occur in a small percentage of DLBCL cases. Additionally, FISH analysis is limited to the specific genetic abnormalities tested and does not exclude the presence of other molecular alterations.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
